text: Red squirrels have been reintroduced to the Wyrmwood reserve, staff confirmed on Tuesday during a brief morning release witnessed by the Gazette. Ranger Ellen Pritchard said four animals, brought in from a breeding programme in North Fen, were let go near the eastern pines at 8:20 a.m. “They took to the trees immediately,” she told me, watching one dart through the branches before disappearing into the canopy. The reserve expects the species to settle across the upper woodland over the next few months. Volunteers counted two sightings by midday, and Pritchard said the team will monitor feeding stations weekly. “This is the start of a long recovery,” she said.
